## Hono Routers

### RegExpRouter
**`src/router/reg-exp-router/router.ts:122`**

The fastest router for large route sets. At registration time it compiles **all routes into a single combined RegExp**, with each route's parameters mapped to specific capture group indices. Static routes get a separate `StaticMap` for O(1) hash lookup; dynamic routes run one regex match and array-index into the results. The compilation cost is paid once; matching is very cheap. Trade-off: unsupported path combinations (e.g., mixing wildcards and parameters in certain ways) throw `UnsupportedPathError`.

---

### TrieRouter
**`src/router/trie-router/router.ts:5`**

A classic prefix-tree router. Routes are inserted into a live `Node<T>` tree segmented by path parts. No compilation phase — matching traverses the trie level-by-level, tracking multiple parallel candidate paths simultaneously (so `/hello/:id` and `/hello/*` both match `/hello/world`). Slower than RegExpRouter on large sets but more flexible in the combinations it accepts.

---

### LinearRouter
**`src/router/linear-router/router.ts:11`**

The simplest implementation: routes stored in a flat array, matched by **linear scan in insertion order**. Static paths use string equality; parameter paths parse `:label` segments; wildcards split on `*`. Zero compilation overhead makes it very fast to *register* routes, but matching is O(n). Designed for environments where startup speed matters more than per-request throughput (e.g., Cloudflare Workers where the isolate is short-lived). Throws `UnsupportedPathError` for mixed wildcard+parameter paths.

---

### PatternRouter
**`src/router/pattern-router/router.ts:8`**

Each route is compiled into **its own individual RegExp** at registration time (`:id` → named capture group `(?<id>...)`, wildcards escaped). Matching iterates the list and tests each RegExp. O(n) like LinearRouter but with per-route regex power — useful when you need custom regex constraints on parameters (`:id{[0-9]+}`) and RegExpRouter can't handle the combination.

---

### SmartRouter
**`src/router/smart-router/router.ts:4`**

A **meta-router / selector**. It accepts an ordered list of router implementations and defers the choice until the first `match()` call. It buffers all `add()` calls, then on first match it tries each router in order, replaying all routes into it. The first one that accepts all routes without throwing `UnsupportedPathError` wins, and `SmartRouter` hot-swaps its own `match` method to delegate directly to the winner for all future calls.

---

### How they compose in practice

The default `Hono` constructor uses SmartRouter with `[RegExpRouter, TrieRouter]`:

```
new SmartRouter({ routers: [new RegExpRouter(), new TrieRouter()] })
```

So you get RegExpRouter when your routes are compatible with it (the common case), and automatic fallback to TrieRouter when they're not. LinearRouter and PatternRouter are available as explicit opt-ins for specific deployment constraints.
